title: Automated batching & caching recommendations with eval-based safe apply/rollback
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Summary:
We need an end-to-end automated flow that recommends batching and prefix/KV caching configuration changes based on workload telemetry, applies those changes safely, and ties any config changes to an automatic quality-regression detection pipeline. The goal is to cut per-token cost by up to 20% on eligible workloads while ensuring no regressions on critical prompts and eval suites.

Problem and rationale:
- Batching and caching are the highest-leverage levers for cost on our hosted and dedicated tiers, but naive application can degrade model output on latency-sensitive or stateful tasks (e.g., multi-turn chat with significant prompt engineering).
- Teams currently make manual config changes and rely on ad-hoc checks. We need a reproducible, auditable path: recommended config -> canary apply -> eval suite run -> automatic pass/fail or rollback.

High-level approach:
1) Recommendation engine: analyze recent 7-day request traces and model usage to propose batching.size, batch_timeout_ms, prefix_cache_enabled, kv_cache_mode, and suggested quantization profile (if applicable). Recommendations are score-ranked by expected cost delta and predicted quality risk. Input signals: token distribution, sequence length histogram, model variant, route-level SLOs, and past eval deltas.
2) Safe apply via controlled rollout: apply changes to a small canary pool (1% of traffic or a dedicated canary GPU pool) with shadowed requests. Run automated evals during the canary window. If metrics are within acceptance thresholds, expand rollout in progressive steps (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%).
3) Eval-based quality gates: run a combination of offline eval suites and online sampled golden-prompt checks. If any threshold breach detected, immediate rollback on the route and a postmortem ticket auto-created.

Eval suite design (what to run):
- Golden prompts: 120 curated prompts per route covering critical flows (e.g., account summarization, legal-text summarization, code generation snippet, instruction-following). These are single-turn and multi-turn variants with expected answers or semantic fingerprints.
- Acceptance metrics: for generation tasks use embedding cosine similarity with golden answer > 0.92 for high-precision flows, > 0.88 for lower-risk flows; for exact-answer tasks require exact match rate >= 98%; for structured outputs validate schema + field-level accuracy >= 95%. For regression-sensitive customers, an additional delta check: no drop > 0.5 points absolute on primary metric.
- Regression detection: compare canary-run metrics against baseline collected over the previous 7 days. Use bootstrapped confidence intervals; require p-value < 0.05 AND absolute delta crossing configured threshold to declare regression.

Safe rollback triggers (examples):
- Golden prompt embedding similarity mean drops by >= 0.03 absolute and affects >5% of golden prompts.
- Exact-match rate drops by >= 1.5 percentage points for exact flows.
- Increase in 5xx/error rate by >0.5% absolute or 100ms median latency increase on the route where SLOs are tight.
- Customer-reported severity: if any verified customer complaint linked to a deployment occurs within the canary window, auto rollback.

Observability & artifacts:
- Canary dashboard (link): https://app.redwood.internal/dashboards/canary-batching-cache (shows golden prompt deltas, eval suite histograms, token cost delta, and traffic percentages).
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1294 (draft - recommendation engine + canary hooks).
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/pages/OPT-automated-batching-caching (metrics, thresholds, diagrams).
- Eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pulls/88 (golden prompt runner + embedding comparator).

Rollout plan and automation details:
- Phase A: offline pilot. Run recommendations in read-only mode; surface top-10 suggestions per week to SRE/owners. No automatic apply.
- Phase B: automated canary apply to a dedicated canary pool with traffic mirroring turned off initially. Run evals for 2 hours, then expand if gates pass.
- Phase C: progressive production rollout with automated monitoring and auto-rollback. Add manual approval step for routes flagged as high-risk.
- Apply mechanism: configs are stored in route-config service. We will add a 'canary_config' field and a rollout controller that swaps in the canary_config on success and writes an audit log.

Data retention and reproducibility:
- Store canary payloads and seed RNGs for each run for 30 days to support postmortems.
- Persist baseline eval snapshots for each route so we can compute deltas reproducibly.

Acceptance criteria (what counts as Done):
- Recommendation engine produces actionable suggestions for at least 80% of non-trivial routes in the pilot org.
- Canary apply workflow can be executed end-to-end via Console or API with a single button/API call.
- Eval harness runs automatically in the canary window and computes the configured metrics.
- Automatic rollback triggers and log an audited event + creates ENG ticket.
- Documentation and runbook published.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Risk of false positives from embedding thresholds when prompts have acceptable semantic paraphrases. Mitigation: multi-metric gates (embedding + token-level ngram overlap + schema checks).
- Cost of running evals on each canary vs. cost savings. We accept an upfront eval compute cost as insurance for production quality.
- How to handle stochastic models where outputs vary across runs: introduce deterministic seeds for eval runs and compare with majority/ensembling tests.

Progress updates / recent activity:
- 2025-02-13: Initial spike complete; baseline metrics schema defined and approved by SRE.
- 2025-02-20: Prototype recommender built that suggests batch_size and prefix_cache_enabled from sequence-length histograms. Achieved median cost savings estimate of 12% on pilot routes.
- 2025-02-28: Eval harness integration PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/88. Needs review from Applied ML and Reliability.
- 2025-03-05: Canary controller MVP merged to runtime with feature flag "auto-config-canary". Draft canary dashboard running at https://app.redwood.internal/dashboards/canary-batching-cache.
- 2025-03-06: Bootstrapping golden-prompt lists for 6 pilot routes completed; need PM review on acceptance thresholds per route.

Reviews and feedback:
- PM review (Samira Chen): requested per-customer override for thresholds and a manual-review gating step for enterprise routes. Action: add per-route policy field in route-config by 2025-03-12.
- Applied ML review (Dr. Nikhil Rao): recommended embedding model v2 for semantic similarity computations; flagged variance issues for code-generation flows. Action: add ensembling + exact-match checks for code routes.
- Design review (Aisha Patel): requested clearer Console UX for canary progression and rollback steps. Action: design mockups due 2025-03-14 (DES-2103).

Follow-up tasks (short):
- Add per-route threshold override UI (PM-342).
- Wire up audit logging + ticket auto-creation on rollback (ENG-4830).
- Run larger pilot across Dedicated pools and measure real cost delta (ENG-4860).
- Expand golden prompt corpus to 400 total prompts covering additional verticals (PM-350).

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-aggressive batching could increase tail latency for real-time workloads. Mitigation: route-level SLO checks; do not recommend batch_size increase for routes with p95 < 100ms target.
- Eval suite coverage gaps. Mitigation: weekly additions and owner sign-off for new routes.

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the acceptance thresholds and rollback triggers; these are the most impactful for safety.
- Check the recommendation features against the telemetry schema in https://docs.redwood.internal/pages/telemetry-schema.
